cards.text: The prophet Jeremiah is still carrying the LORD's message about Babylon (Jeremiah 50:1), and it is NOT good news for Babylon. Right in the middle of it, the LORD calls out to His own people.

cards.question: The LORD calls out to His people living in Babylon. What does He tell them to do?
The LORD also tells each of His people to save their ___ from His fierce anger.

cards.text: Then He tells them about news that's coming: a rumor one year, another the next, of violence in the land and ruler against ruler.

cards.question: When those rumors of violence and ruler against ruler come, the LORD tells His people not to be afraid.

cards.text: The days are coming when the LORD will punish Babylon's idols. Her whole land will suffer shame, and her slain will lie fallen within her.

cards.question: When the destroyers from the north come against Babylon, heaven and earth will mourn over her.

cards.text: Then comes the reason, plain as day: 'Babylon must fall on account of the slain of Israel…'

cards.question: Babylon's end comes on account of the slain of Israel. What does the verse say about the slain of all the earth?

answers.text: They will be avenged by Israel

cards.text: Then the call goes out: 'You who have escaped the sword, depart and do not linger!' No snooze button on this one, friend.

cards.question: The ones who escaped the sword are told to leave Babylon without lingering. What are they told to keep in mind from far away?

cards.text: Then comes a new line, and it's heavy: 'We are ashamed because we have heard reproach; disgrace has covered our faces…'

cards.question: Why do the speakers say disgrace has covered their faces?

answers.text: Foreigners entered the LORD's holy places
Their own king abandoned the city
Their harvest failed two years running

cards.text: Then the LORD says it again: the days are coming when He will punish Babylon's idols, and throughout her land the wounded will groan.

cards.question: Even if Babylon climbs to the heavens and fortifies her lofty stronghold, the destroyers the LORD sends will still come against her.

cards.text: Then listen: the sound of a cry comes from Babylon, the sound of great destruction from the land of the Chaldeans, Babylon's people.

cards.question: The LORD is going to destroy Babylon. What does He say He'll do to her mighty voice?

cards.text: And there's more noise: the waves will roar like great waters, and the tumult of their voices will resound.
A destroyer is coming against Babylon. Her warriors will be captured and their bows broken.

cards.question: Babylon's warriors will be captured and their bows broken, for the LORD is a God of retribution. What does the verse say He will do?

answers.text: He will give her more time

cards.text: Then the LORD says He'll make her princes and wise men drunk, along with her governors, officials and warriors. That's the WHOLE org chart, friend, from the corner office all the way down to the front desk.

cards.question: After the LORD makes Babylon's leaders drunk, they will sleep it off and wake up the next morning.
This word about Babylon's leaders is declared by the King. What name does the verse give the King?

cards.text: Then the LORD of Hosts speaks about her defenses: Babylon's thick walls will be leveled. Thick walls, friend, and they're coming DOWN.

cards.question: Babylon's thick walls will be leveled. What will happen to her high gates?
With Babylon's walls leveled and her gates burned, the LORD of Hosts says the work the people put into her will last for generations.

cards.text: The people's labor will be for nothing, and the nations will exhaust themselves to fuel the flames. That's like working overtime all month and watching the boss hit DELETE on your project.
